text: Gold held roughly flat near $3,857 on Tuesday morning after Monday's slide to about $3,830, its lowest since October 2025.
Silver rebounded about 1.7% to near $47.70 from Monday's 14-month low, easing the gold/silver ratio to about 80.9 from 82.3.
US October retail sales rose 0.2%, in line with forecasts and slower than September's 0.8%, while core sales rose 0.6%, more than the 0.4% expected.
Stock futures were mixed to slightly lower ahead of Nvidia's earnings after the close, following Monday's third straight drop for the S&P 500.
Treasury yields were little changed before the data (10-year near 5.12%, 2-year down 2 bp to about 4.81%).
The yen firmed about 0.2% to near 159.1 per dollar on haven demand and intervention worries, while the dollar index held flat near its highest since April 2025.
Brent crude slipped another 0.7% to about $91.80 as worries about a supply surplus continued.
